findings.finding: Hippo's own FY2026 guide leaves a soft second half. FY adjusted net income of $62-70M less 1H's $38.2M leaves $23.8-31.8M for Q3+Q4, ~$12-16M a quarter, against Q2-26 $21.0M (6.7% cat ratio) and Q3-25 $18.3M (0.0% cat). The FY 10% cat ratio against 1H's 5.7% implies a second-half cat budget of roughly 13-14% of NEP. A Q3 cat ratio in the single digits would therefore beat the guide's implied run-rate and set up a third FY raise this year (the guide was raised in both Q1 and Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raises have been bought: Q2-26 (Jul 30, GWP/revenue/combined-ratio/adj NI all raised) +6.87%; Q2-25 +14.03%; Q3-25 +5.46%. Prints without a meaningful raise were sold: Q1-26 -6.70% despite an EPS beat, Q4-25 -4.89%.
findings.why_not_priced: The partial pricing is visible in the +23% 20-day run-up to near the 52-week high. But the EPS consensus is scattered from $0.27 to $0.68, so the street has not converged on the guide-implied second-half run-rate. If the market had fully priced a third raise, the bar would sit near Q2's $0.79 and the sources would agree.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 industry cat losses were concentrated away from Hippo's largest state. Gallagher Re (Oct 21) puts nine-month global insured losses at the lowest since 2019 and US SCS at $43B YTD. Q3's big events were the Plains/Midwest/Mid-Atlantic outbreak of Aug 9-12 and Chicago/Ohio Valley storms, the Spokane wildfire (~$1B), and Hawaii hurricanes, with no major US hurricane landfall in Q3. Moody's had Texas hail reports down ~70% in 1H-26 against 2023-25. Texas (18%) and California (18%) are Hippo's top states by Q2 GWP. This is a proxy for a lighter-than-budget Hippo Q3 cat ratio.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2-26, Hippo printed a 6.7% cat ratio in a heavy industry SCS quarter and the stock rose 6.87% on that print with a raise. In Q3-24 (Beryl, Texas) the cat ratio was 22.8% and the stock fell (Nov-24 print, outside the 7-event baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Hippo does not pre-announce cats and no analyst publishes a Hippo-specific Q3 cat estimate that I could find. If it were priced, the scattered EPS bar would have converged upward. This is weather-to-company inference, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Moody's on 1H Texas/Colorado hail: https://www.moodys.com/web/en/us/insights/insurance/united-states-severe-convective-storm-losses-quieter-and-less-costly-during-first-half-2026.html; August storm geography: https://www.intelligentinsurer.com/us-scs-losses-top-dollar35bn-year-to-date-as-august-storms-add-billions. Hippo's state mix comes from the Q2 release (same document as finding 1). Proxy only.

findings.finding: Personal-lines peers took much heavier Q3 cats year on year. Allstate's Q3-26 pre-tax cats were $1.65B (July $682M, August $748M, September $220M), nearly three times the $558M of Q3-25. Travelers' Personal Insurance cat ratio was 9.2 points against 6.0. Hippo's Q3-25 cat ratio was 0.0%, so its reported Q3 cat and combined ratio will almost certainly be worse year on year even if they come in inside the guide's budget.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3-25 (0% cat, combined ratio 100.0%) rose 5.46%. Travelers fell ~4.4% premarket on Oct 16, 2026 on a beat with higher year-on-year cats.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: Allstate's monthly releases and the Travelers print are public, and the Q3 cat would land inside a guide that already embeds a heavy second-half budget. The residual is a headline year-on-year deterioration against a 0.0% comparison.
findings.independence: Travelers Q3-26 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000086312/000008631226000181/trv-20260930.htm. Partly offsets finding 2, which rests on different sources (geography versus national peer totals).

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias, the first major hurricane of 2026, made landfall as a Category 2 near Destin on Florida's Panhandle on Oct 9, 2026. Insured loss estimates run from $1-2B (Verisk) to $3.5B best estimate (Moody's RMS); Florida regulators counted 46,509 claims and $582M by Oct 15. Florida was 12% of Hippo's Q2 GWP. Management will have to frame Q4 cat against the 10% FY budget on this call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no Hippo print with an in-quarter hurricane commentary in the 7-event baseline. Q3-24 (Beryl) was a large miss.
findings.why_not_priced: The storm is public, but Hippo's Florida exposure is mostly partner/fronted business at low net retention, and the new Group CAT program's retention is undisclosed. The market cannot size Hippo's net hit until management speaks. If it were priced in full, the run-up would not have continued through mid-October (from ~$35 on Oct 17 to $37.91).
findings.independence: Moody's RMS estimate: https://www.businessinsurance.com/moodys-rms-puts-hurricane-isaias-best-estimate-at-3-5b/. Gallagher Re says it falls outside the nine-month window (Artemis link in finding 2).

findings.finding: The Accelerant fronting program (>$500M of 2027 GWP) fully commenced on Oct 1, 2026, so the Q3 call is the first at which Hippo can quantify Q4 fronted GWP and frame 2027. Accelerant itself agreed on Aug 13, 2026 to be taken private by Thoma Bravo (>$4B, $20.25/share), a change of control at Hippo's largest new fronting counterparty that the call may address.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The June 30 Accelerant announcement and the Q2 GWP raise preceded the +6.87% Jul-26 reaction; the GWP line has been a positive driver.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the program was announced in June and partly embedded in the July GWP raise. The unpriced part is a 2027 number or a Q4 GWP update. The Thoma Bravo deal has drawn no Hippo-specific commentary in the wire.
findings.independence: Thoma Bravo release: https://www.thomabravo.com/press-releases/accelerant-enters-into-definitive-agreement-to-be-acquired-by-thoma-bravo. On the Q2 call management said Accelerant premium will be 'in excess of $500 million next year' (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-30-hippo-holdings-inc-stock/).

baseline_tension: The fundamental lean (guide-implied soft second half, light Texas cat quarter, raises bought) is positive. It cuts against the +35-point put skew and sits on top of a +23% run-up into the 52-week high at the consensus target. The skew is on a 319-OI, 37%-spread chain, which is my reason for not deferring to it fully, but together they pull p_up from 56 to 55 and leave the findings sum small (+0.6).
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (proxy and weather inference loses to documents): Q3 industry-geography cat finding cut from +1.0 to +0.5, and the peer-cat finding from -0.5 to -0.4. Both are filed as proxies.
Lesson 6 (bar): the EPS bar is disputed across four sources ($0.27-$0.68), so findings are sized against the company guide and a three-source revenue bar, and EPS-dependent sizing stays capped.

Lesson 7 (positioning and skew): the sign runs against a +35-vol-point put skew, so p_up moved from 56 to 55 (expected move 1.2 to 1.0). The reason given is the chain's illiquidity. Short interest was checked: not crowded.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): the guidance finding is kept at +2.0 because this name's reaction history pays for raises; no further cut.
